title: Dense or bounded simulation of hard-to-invert leakage
summary: Determine whether Dodis--Kalai--Lovett hard-to-invert leakage is dense leakage or can otherwise be simulated from bounded leakage with good parameters.

formal_statement.body: Let $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{HTI}}$ be the hard-to-invert auxiliary-input leakage family of Dodis, Kalai, and Lovett cited by the source. Prove either that $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{HTI}}$ is contained in the source's dense-leakage class, or that every leakage in $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{HTI}}$ admits the source's bounded-leakage simulation with quantitatively good leakage length and statistical error. Otherwise, establish an obstruction to both alternatives.

scope.domain: Simulation of hard-to-invert auxiliary-input leakage in dense and bounded leakage models
assumptions: Hard-to-invert leakage is the Dodis--Kalai--Lovett family cited as reference [62] in the TIT restatement
Dense leakage and bounded-leakage simulation use the source's definitions and quantitative guarantees
scope.unresolved_remainder: No inspected later primary text proves dense-family containment, supplies the requested bounded-leakage simulation theorem, or rules out both alternatives for the Dodis--Kalai--Lovett family.

provenance.note: The TIT article identifies the EUROCRYPT 2021 preliminary version; the same exact open questions are text-confirmed in IACR ePrint 2020/1246, submitted on 2020-10-09.
